label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

The `handleClick` handler calls `exportReport(...).then(...)` but never attaches a `.catch()`. When the export request fails (non-2xx response, or the fetch rejecting), the promise rejects, `setBusy(false)` is never reached, and the button remains disabled until the page is reloaded. The fix is to handle the rejection (e.g. wrap in try/catch or add `.catch()`) and reset `busy` to `false` while showing an error toast.

input.title: Re-enable the export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

In handleClick, exportReport(...).then(() => { setBusy(false); ... }) only clears the busy state on success. If the fetch rejects (e.g. a non-2xx response throws), setBusy(false) is never called, so the button stays disabled until the page is reloaded. Add a .catch (or a try/finally around an async handler) that resets busy to false and surfaces an error toast on failure, so a failed export leaves the button clickable again.
